findings.claim: PageImages.close() gives up when PYMUPDF_LOCK cannot be acquired within the remaining budget and drops the open pymupdf Document, so its finalizer (fz_drop_document) runs outside the lock while another thread (the extraction holding the lock) is using MuPDF.
findings.impact: When a page request coincides with a long PDF extraction or page OCR (uploading or reindexing PDFs while asking), MuPDF runs from two threads at once. pdf.py:60-62 says this makes a conversion fail over to plain text or return wrong text, so the indexed text of the other PDF can be silently wrong.
findings.evidence: addons/intelligence/app/rag/file_question.py:1038-1051: `if not PYMUPDF_LOCK.acquire(timeout=max(0.0, self._end - time.monotonic())): return` and the comment says 'the garbage collector closes the document'. `document` is a local, so CPython drops it when close() returns, in the worker thread and without the lock. The case is reached whenever open() succeeded and an extraction took the lock afterwards: for example image() raises lock_timeout, the budget is then spent, and acquire(timeout=0) fails at once. Also file_question.py:1026-1032: `return pixmap.tobytes("jpeg")` inside `with self._locked()` releases the lock before the Page and Pixmap locals are freed, so their MuPDF drops also run unlocked on every render. page_ocr.py:158-162 already leaves `page` outside its lock, so that half of the pattern is pre-existing in the addon.
findings.repro: not_reproduced. Mutation view: test_every_pymupdf_call_for_a_page_image_holds_the_lock patches only Document.__init__ and Page.get_pixmap, and test_a_lock_held_past_thirty_seconds holds the lock before open(), so no Document exists and close() returns early. No test opens the document, takes the lock away and then checks close or deallocation, so a close() with no lock at all would also pass.

bucket_proposal.reason: I8 requires every PyMuPDF call made to render page images to run while holding PYMUPDF_LOCK. Closing or dropping the document and the page or pixmap is such a call, and here it runs unlocked.

findings.proposed_fix: Wait for the lock without a timeout in close(), or hand the Document to a holder that drops it under the lock. Free page and pixmap (`del page, pixmap` after computing the bytes) before leaving the locked block.

findings.claim: page_image_path calls config.resolve_stored_path (NFC/NFD on-disk spelling) as well as joining settings.drive_mounts. config.py is listed only for `settings.drive_mounts`, and a stored absolute path is returned without that normalisation.
findings.impact: A PDF stored with an absolute path whose on-disk name is NFD-decomposed cannot be opened, so every page is 'not available', while the same file stored relative is found.
findings.evidence: addons/intelligence/app/rag/file_question.py:987-996: `if os.path.isabs(material.file_path): return material.file_path` and `return config.resolve_stored_path(config.resolve_file_path(...))`. config.py:1294 resolve_stored_path explains why the join alone is not enough.

bucket_proposal.reason: It reaches a config helper beyond the declared read-only use and treats the two path forms unevenly. No invariant is broken; the pages are named 'not available' as I7 allows.

findings.proposed_fix: Pass the absolute path through config.resolve_stored_path too.

findings.claim: On the final request, once a whitespace-only first delta arrives, _answer_with_keepalive stops writing keep-alives (first=False), and the document loop holds that delta without writing an answer_chunk. The stream can then stay silent past 5 s before the first answer_chunk.
findings.impact: A reasoning model that emits a leading newline and then pauses can leave the SSE line silent long enough for a proxy idle timeout to close it. The viewer then sees the answer fail.
findings.evidence: addons/intelligence/app/routers/rag.py:2864-2875 (`first = False` after any delta; then `timeout=None`); the final branch of _document_tool_answer holds whitespace deltas (`held = [*held, delta]; if not "".join(held).strip(): continue`), so no answer_chunk and no keep-alive is written.

bucket_proposal.reason: Spec §1.6 requires a keep-alive at least every 5 s until the first answer_chunk. That is a required item, not a declared invariant.

findings.proposed_fix: In the held state, read with a keep-alive timeout as well, for example by tracking 'first visible chunk written' in place of 'first delta'.

findings.claim: An EPUB contents line writes the stored section title cut to 60 characters with no removal of `[n]` markers or line breaks, so a title such as '[1] Introduction' puts a bracketed number on a line that names a section.
findings.impact: The prompt pairs a section with a passage-like number, which is the confusion I5 and SPEC-ADDON-114 I11 keep out, so the model may cite [1] for the wrong place. A title with a newline also splits a contents line.
findings.evidence: addons/intelligence/app/rag/file_question.py document_contents: `f"{label}: {title[:DOCUMENT_TITLE_CHARS]} — {excerpt}"`. Only the excerpt goes through _without_markers (in _document_excerpt).

bucket_proposal.reason: I5: every line the prompt writes itself that names a section carries no bracketed number. The title is part of a line the prompt composes.

findings.proposed_fix: Remove `[1-3 digits]` markers and collapse whitespace in the title before cutting it, as the excerpt does.

specification_compliance: I1: uses_document_tools (file_question.py:356) and the branch in _file_question_stream match: can_see and (PDF, or EPUB with partial). _document_tools orders get_text before get_page_images.

I2: served is capped at _FRAME_REQUESTS_PER_QUESTION. The final request uses tool_choice none. Tool replies are awaited whole before anything is written. Deadline checks are at the loop top, in _until_done and in asyncio.timeout.
I3: _serve_text_request writes whole rows and names sent rows by number. The length check counts the reserve; the first row is always written. The note names the last number written.

I7: the per-call limit is 4. Pages are judged against the PDF's own page_count, and sent_pages stops repeats. The zoom makes the long edge 1280 px. Failures take no number.
I8: open, page_count and render run under the lock. Close on timeout and object deallocation do not (CR-1).
I9: no writes found. Logs carry the exception class and file id only.

potential_unspecified_behavior.behavior: When the lock cannot be retaken within the budget, the opened PDF is left to the garbage collector to close, outside PYMUPDF_LOCK.
potential_unspecified_behavior.reason: A page request during a long PDF extraction can make the other PDF's extraction silently return wrong text.

potential_unspecified_behavior.behavior: A relative stored path is resolved to its on-disk NFC/NFD spelling; an absolute one is not.
potential_unspecified_behavior.reason: An absolute-path PDF with a decomposed name gets every page 'not available'.

potential_unspecified_behavior.behavior: Keep-alives stop on the final request after a whitespace-only first delta, until visible text arrives.
potential_unspecified_behavior.reason: A model that pauses after a leading newline can leave the line silent past a proxy timeout, and the answer fails.

potential_unspecified_behavior.behavior: A PDF whose rows store no readable page gets contents lines that are ranges only, and get_text by page answers 'Nothing is written from page N on.' although text exists.
potential_unspecified_behavior.reason: For such a PDF, the model can read more only through `after`.

potential_unspecified_behavior.behavior: EPUB section titles enter the contents with their bracketed numbers and line breaks kept.
potential_unspecified_behavior.reason: A title like '[1] Intro' places a citation-like number beside a section.

potential_unspecified_behavior.behavior: A cut PDF with neither a pdf_markdown row nor any page unit tells the model 'a page number from 1 to 0' and states no page count.
potential_unspecified_behavior.reason: It needs rows with no page and no markdown row; the model can still use `after`.
